text:
Predicates:
BakedSweet(x) ::: x is a baked sweet.
Spicy(x) ::: x is spicy.
Cupcake(x) ::: x is a cupcake.
MalaHotpot(x) ::: x is a mala hotpot.
Product(x, y) ::: x is a product of y.
Premises:
¬∃x (BakedSweet(x) ∧ Spicy(x)) ::: No baked sweets are spicy.
∀x (Cupcake(x) → BakedSweet(x)) ::: All cupcakes are baked sweets.
∀x (MalaHotpot(x) → Spicy(x)) ::: All mala hotpots are spicy.
∀x (Product(x, bakedByMelissa) → Cupcake(x)) ::: All products from Baked by Melissa are cupcakes.
Spicy(driedThaiChilies) ⊕ MalaHotpot(driedThaiChilies) ⊕ ¬BakedSweet(driedThaiChilies) ::: Dried Thai chilies are spicy or mala hotpots or not baked sweets.
Conclusion:
Product(driedThaiChilies, bakedByMelissa) ::: Dried Thai chilies are products of Baked by Melissa.
